/blog/smart-devices-connection.html.bodyHtml:
A smart home is an auto system that integrates all devices in your house, whether wiring or wireless. The smart device makes life simple by virtually controlling any device in the home, from your lights, fans, television, music system, etc. Smart devices can be very effective in Saving Energy Costs, Adding Security, Saving you time, and adding convenience. It provides excellent comfort, pleasure, and well-being.

Greenhse technologies offer you different types of Smart home devices for your home. Let's have a look at Smart lighting products.

Today, in this article, you'll learn all about Smart Devices, how to purchase them, and how to install and manage them from app and app functionality.

Tip to Purchase Smart device

Purchase smart items that use generic and not proprietary apps. Proprietary apps will lock you into contracts, often be more expensive, and most likely not be available or supported in the future. Purchase products from local suppliers, or at least suppliers in your country, as there is a greater chance these will work. Smart products that work in some countries are not guaranteed to work everywhere. Local purchases will also have support services, as well as replacement or refund options. Not all smart items are the same, even if they are called the same name and look for more information.

The smart functions can be limited on certain products to save costs and mislead buyers, and output and specifications can also be lower, ie; Smart plugs can have remote switching, multiple timers, energy monitoring, and countdown options. They can also connect to other smart devices and be controlled by numerous sensors or switches. A proprietary smart plug, will only be able to connect to proprietary devices, may have limited timer control and no energy monitoring, yet look the same and be called the same name.

Smart lights with warm to cool white and full-colour dimming options may also have functions enabling them to work with Alexa or Google, timers, and other smart devices, yet some may only have the basic functions with ⅓ the brightness level in full colour models. Smart IP cameras can also vary a lot. The resolution, recording functions, and sensor capabilities can vary greatly and some requiring ongoing fees every month or year.

Smart Device Installation tips

The main problem with connecting and Installation is a lack of understanding of your Router and how to ensure this is set up correctly and easy installation of smart products. The second biggest problem is badly written and misleading instructions. This article is to assist you with these 2 points. ROUTER (OR MODEM) TIPS: Our Modems convert our internet signal according to our service provider, our Router enables this converted signal to be sent to our devices using WIFI. Most Routers are Dual band, using both the 2.4GHz and 5 GHz frequency range.

Unfortunately most smart devices only work with the 2,4GHz frequency range, and in-order to get our devices to connect to our Router, we often need to make some changes to ensure devices can be added. Log on to the Router using information on the router label. ie. “10.1.1.1” and password “admin” (or new password chosen previously).

5GHz is not the same as 5G, 2.4GHz and 5GHz refer to the operating frequency of the device. 5G refers to fifth Generation, which came after 4G (fourth Generation) which came after 3G (third generation) ….and does not refer to frequency, although different frequency and wavelengths are used for the different generations. If your Router is set up with both a 2.4GHz and a 5GHz option with different names and passwords, select the 2,4GHz option (or non 5GHz option) on your smart phone and then add the smart device using the same 2,4GHz name and password. If both the 2.4GHz and 5GHz options use the same name and password, log onto the router, create these as 2 separate names and passwords and then select the 2.4GHz option.

Also read: How To Change 5GHz To 2.4GHz To Connect Smart Devices

NB: both the smart phone and smart device being added must both use the same 2.4GHz network while setting up. After this stage it is fairly easy (in most cases) to connect. The next most common issue would be ensuring that the device is ready for pairing and that the indicator light or device is flashing correctly as per the instructions, on the App.

/blog/smart-kinetic-rf-switches.html.bodyHtml:
SMART Kinetic RF switches, offered by Greenhse Technologies, are the best choice for smart homes due to their unparalleled advantages. These wireless switches offer effortless installation, eliminating the need for complex wiring and making them perfect for retrofitting existing homes. Their energy efficiency allows for reduced power consumption and automated scheduling, optimizing energy usage and lowering electricity bills. With reliable and responsive RF technology, Smart Kinetic RF switches ensure seamless communication within a smart home, even through walls and obstacles. Their flexibility and scalability allow for easy relocation and expansion as smart home needs evolve. Compatible with various smart home ecosystems, these switches integrate effortlessly, providing convenient control through voice assistants or dedicated mobile apps.

Watch the video: Kinetic RF Switches

 

CHARACTERISTICS OF KINETIC RF SWITCHES

  1. Kinetic switches require no connected wires, or even batteries.
  2. They connect directly to a receiving Module placed in the ceiling near the lights or device.
  3. Available in 1, 2 & 3 gang, they are attractive, very strong, neat and completely waterproof, IP67
  4. These switches can connect to various different control modules;- 1000W Receiver Dual 1200W Receiver (600W x 2) Dimmer 100W Receiver Smart 600W Receiver Smart Dimmer 100W Receiver
  5. Depending on the receiver Module selected, Kinetic switches can turn devices ON/OFF, DIM and even with SMART Control.
  6. With no wiring required, construction cost savings are possible but more importantly you have complete flexibility and no limitations. Switches can be added as and where required.
  7. 2-Way and 3-way switching work well with this system. Multiple switches can link to one receiver, and multiple receivers can link to one switch.
  8. Perfect for bed side tables and island benches
  9. Suitable for outdoor areas
  10. Even suitable for wheelchairs and special requirements.

 

Check out our wide range Smart Switches collection here.

 

PAIRING KINETIC SWITCHES TO RECEIVER MODULES

  1. Once receiver Module has been wired, push the square linking button until the red light flashes slowly. Let go, then push the Kinetic switch that is being linked to it once quickly and let go. (Be careful to not push the incorrect switch as un-linking is more difficult.)
  2. To unlink, the Square button needs to be pushed for about 12 seconds. The red light will flash slowly, then it will flash quickly, then it will stop flashing. then stop pushing the square button and the switch will be unlinked.
  3. Dual receiver Module - can connect to 2 separate devices with different switches. Connecting the first device to the first switch is the same as all receivers. Push for 3 seconds until red light flashes, let go and push kinetic switch once quickly and let go.
  4. To connect the second device, push square button twice quickly and the light will turn BLUE. Push and hold square button for 3 seconds and BLUE light will flash. Push the second Kinetic switch once quickly to pair second switch to second output on the receiver Module. To get back to the RED light, push square button twice quickly.
  5. Note: Multiple switches can be linked to a single receiver and multiple receivers can be linked to 1 switch. Carefully plan and link correctly, or incorrect switching will occur and unlinking will be required. For the dual controller Both RED and BLUE channels may need to be unlinked.
  6. SMART receivers will need to be linked to the home WiFi.
  7. When the Smart Receiver Module is turned on the Red light will flash quickly. Open the Smart Life or Tuya App and push “+” add device.
  8. The receiver Module will open on the App, select ‘Add device’. Once added, select and change the name.
  9. If the “Smart Dimmer” module has been added, set the “minimum level” to ensure light can be seen and no flickering.
  10. After Smart receivers have been added they can be linked to a Kinetic switch by pushing the “+ Pair” button, then pushing the Kinetic switch you want to link to it - once.
  11. With the Smart receivers linked to the WiFi and Kinetic switches, numerous options are available using the “Scene” function on the bottom of the App page.

 

HOW TO CONNECT AND SET UP KINETIC RF SWITCHES

  1. Ensure your WiFi is set up and working well, and if you plan on using more than 10 Smart device, invest in a good WiFi extender, such as the UBIQUITI U6-LR.
  2. Set up a separate 2.4GHz network with its own name and password, or ask your provider, or WiFi supplier to set this up before leaving. Please use a name and password you can remember correctly and get right each time.
  3. Load and register “Smart Life” or “Tuya” App.
  4. Select the 2.4GHz WiFi selection on your Smart device and ensure you have good WiFi strength where the device will be added (3 bars or more on signal strength).
  5. Follow the product installation instructions and use the same 2.4GHz name and password.

Overall, Smart Kinetic RF switches combine convenience, efficiency, reliability, and versatility, making them the optimal choice for modern smart homes offered by Greenhse Technologies, the best LED Lighting Shop in Ellenbrook Perth.

/blog/smart-switches-everything-you-need.h1: Crystal Glass Switches - Everything you need to know before ordering
/blog/smart-switches-everything-you-need.lede: Crystal touch switch plates and smart switches can enhance the aesthetics and functionality of a Smart Home Perth.
/blog/smart-switches-everything-you-need.bodyHtml:
Crystal touch switch plates and smart switches can enhance the aesthetics and functionality of a Smart Home Perth. These are elegant and easy to clean, with attractive soft lighting to indicate ON/OFF, and are easy to see in the dark. However, there are certain requirements and a few limitations so please follow the guidelines below before ordering:

STANDARD SWITCHES:

  1. Standard touch switches are single-wire and do not require a Neutral
  2. Available in 1, 2, 3 & 4 Gang switches
  3. Two-way switching is available in 1, 2 & 3 gangs, using standard communication wiring. 2 x two-way switches will be required (any number of gangs) and these get paired electronically after installation
  4. Dimmer and non-dimmer switches on 1 plate are not available
  5. 1, 2 & 3 gang dimmers are available, but all lights need to be dimmable
  6. With single wiring on electronic switches there can be interference from lighting circuits and 1 x Load correction device on the circuit (normally installed in the first socket) may be required
  7. Load correction devices can assist with dimming and residual current which causes some LED globes to glow when switched off
  8. Smart lights require a load correction device on the circuit; this assists with stability and maintains the live circuit when using the App

SMART SWITCHES:

  1. Smart switches require Neutral wires
  2. 1, 2, 3 & 4 Gang switches are available
  3. Curtain/blind Switches are available
  4. 1 Gang dimmable switches are available
  5. Smart switches are more stable because they are neutral. Load correction devices are not required
  6. Smart switches can be linked to do 2-Way and 3-way Switching with no additional wiring
  7. Smart switches can be switched ON/OFF remotely with smart devices and can work with sensors, cameras, Alexa, Google etc.
  8. Smart switches can also be linked to remote sockets or switches with no wiring

TIPS:

  1. When building a new Smart Home Perth, always allow for Neutral wires or conduits wherever you may require a smart switch
  2. Smart switches are very useful at the front door, as security cameras can be linked to switches on lights for convenience and safety at no extra cost
  3. Smart switches can also enable you to add gangs and link to other switches, or garden lights etc. with no extra cabling
  4. Smart switches can be combined with standard switches as they look and feel the same. This will save costs as Smart switches are not really required in most applications

What do you do if you have no Neutral wires or Conduits:

  1. Electricians can often add a Neutral wire to switches on external walls as these can be double brick with a cavity between them
  2. Neutral wires can be added if there is a garage, cupboard or area behind the switch wall that will not be affected by running an external conduit
  3. Two-way cabling can be converted to a Neutral with correct testing and heat-shrinking the exposed cable ends to Blue
  4. Circuits can be combined, and the extra cable converted to a Neutral
  5. Remember extra switches can be added using smart receivers or sockets without any wiring

After reading this, order your smart switches requirement today so that one of our Greenhse experts or recommended electricians can assist you further. Please note we can only supply recommendations, and it is advisable to discuss your options with your electrician and for them to call us direct.

/blog/ubiquiti-wifi-extender-setup-guide.h1: Ubiquiti WIFI Extender Setup: Complete Connection Guide
/blog/ubiquiti-wifi-extender-setup-guide.lede: What is Ubiquiti WiFi Extender? A Ubiquiti WiFi Extender is a powerful device designed to improve your wireless network's range and performance.
/blog/ubiquiti-wifi-extender-setup-guide.bodyHtml:
What is Ubiquiti WiFi Extender?

A Ubiquiti WiFi Extender is a powerful device designed to improve your wireless network's range and performance. Unlike standard routers, this extender uses advanced technology to eliminate dead zones in your home or office, ensuring consistent connectivity. It is especially useful in larger spaces where the signal from your existing modem or router struggles to reach certain areas. By acting as a bridge between your router and devices, the Ubiquiti WiFi Extender allows for uninterrupted internet access, even in challenging environments.

 

Benefits of using Ubiquiti WIFI Extender

Using a Ubiquiti WiFi Extender offers several benefits, particularly for users with high internet demands. First, it significantly boosts the number of devices connecting simultaneously, from about 12 to up to 300. This makes it ideal for smart homes or offices where multiple devices are constantly in use. Second, it enhances signal strength and speed, providing a seamless experience for streaming, gaming, or video conferencing. Lastly, it supports dual-band frequencies (2.4GHz and 5GHz), ensuring flexibility and compatibility with various devices. With its central placement under the ceiling, the extender ensures optimal signal distribution throughout your space.

Watch the video below for a hassle-free guide to connecting your Ubiquiti WiFi Extender.

How to connect Ubiquiti WIFI Extender

1. Unbox the device: Remove the device from its packaging and ensure you have all the necessary components, including power adapters and cables. Ubiquiti uses P.O.E (Power Over Ethernet), so you will require the correct P.O.E power supply.

2. Connect to Power and Data: Connect a data cable from the original modem/router to the POE adapter, then run the data cable to the Ubiquiti device. Ideally, place the device centrally in your home, under the ceiling (data cables are usually run through the ceiling space).

3. Prepare for Installation: Before installing, take a clear picture of the barcode on the back of the Ubiquiti device, as you’ll need it later for app configuration.

4. Install the UBIQUITI App: Download and open the Ubiquiti App. Select "Add Device" and scan the barcode when prompted.

5. Configure the Device: Once added, configure the Wi-Fi name and password for both 2.4GHz and 5GHz frequencies.

6. Optimize Device Settings: If multiple devices are connected to your existing router, use the same Wi-Fi name and password for the Ubiquiti extender to maintain continuity.

7. Disable Original Wi-Fi: After setup, switch off the Wi-Fi on your original modem/router to fully utilize the extender's capabilities.

With the Ubiquiti WiFi Extender, you can enjoy enhanced internet connectivity and seamless operation of your smart devices. Greenhse Technologies is your go-to destination for the best LED lighting products and smart home solutions in Perth. Shop now to upgrade your lifestyle!

/blog/understanding-strip-lighting-guide.h1: Understanding Strip Lighting  - A Practical Guide to Choosing the Right Solution
/blog/understanding-strip-lighting-guide.lede: Learn how to choose the right strip lighting product for your space. Explore types, features, and expert tips from Greenhse Technologies' trusted lighting store in Perth.
/blog/understanding-strip-lighting-guide.bodyHtml:
Strip lighting is one of the most versatile and powerful lighting solutions available today. It allows you to create stunning architectural features while also delivering highly functional, practical lighting.

However, there is no single strip light that does everything. The reason there are so many options (often 40+ types) is simple — each one is designed for a specific purpose, with its own strengths and limitations.

This guide by Greenhse Perth breaks down the key factors to help you confidently choose the right strip lighting for your application. 

1. Length & Run Capability

One of the most important considerations is how far your strip lighting needs to run.

  • 12V Strip Lighting
    • Higher current, shorter run lengths
    • Suitable for small applications
  • 24V Strip Lighting
    • Lower current and reduced heat
    • Typically up to 5 metres per run
  • Long-Run 24V Strip
    • Up to 20 metres from one end
    • Up to 40 metres when powered from both ends
    • No visible voltage drop
  • 240V Strip Lighting
    • Ideal for very long runs (up to 50 metres)
    • Minimal voltage drop and lower heat
    • No driver required

2. Colour Options

Colour selection impacts both aesthetics and functionality.

  • RGB (Full Colour)
    • Millions of colour options
    • White light is created by mixing colours (often less natural)
  • CCT (Tunable White)
    • Adjustable white light (typically 2700K–6500K)
    • Ideal for spaces requiring colour flexibility
  • Single Colour
    • Consistent, high-quality white light
    • Available in common tones:
      • 2700K (Warm)
      • 3000K (Warm White)
      • 4000K (Neutral)
      • 5500K–6000K (Cool/Daylight)

Key points:
 If you want quality white light → choose Single Colour or CCT
 If you want effects → choose RGB

3. Brightness & Performance

Brightness is measured in lumens, not watts.

  • Higher wattage generally = more light
  • Efficiency matters more than power
  • Strip lights with 150 lumens/Watt or higher will not only produce more light, but also lower power bills.

Typical Performance Range

  • Greenhse have strip lights from 7.5W/m with 700 lumens to 23W/m with over 3500 Lumens/meter.

(As a reference a standard 8-10Watt Downlighting has about 900 lumens) 

  • Entry level: ~700 lumens/m
  • High performance: 3500+ lumens/m

Practical Guidelines

  • Display lighting / niches: High brightness required
  • Under-cabinet (2–3m):
    • ~12W/m
    • 1800+ lumens/m ideal

Dimming

  • All strip lights can be dimmed
  • Down to <5% brightness
  • Improves energy efficiency and control

Key Points:
 Focus on lumens and efficiency, not just wattage.

4. Quality Matters

Quality affects appearance, performance, and lifespan.

Key Factors:

  • LED Density
    • Higher density = smoother, dot-free light
  • CRI (Colour Rendering Index)
    • CRI 90+ = accurate, vibrant colours
    • CRI 70 = lower quality output
  • PCB Construction
    • 10mm PCB = stronger and more durable than 5mm
    • 3 OZZ (3 x PCB copper layers)= better heat handling and longevity
  • Efficiency
    • 160 lm/W uses significantly less power than 80 lm/W
  • Voltage
    • 24V = lower heat and longer lifespan vs 12V
  • Coatings
    • Improve durability and weather resistance
    • Chip design and edging can prevent light separation
  • Warranty
    • Premium strips offer up to 5 years

Key takeaway:
 Better quality = better light, longer life, and fewer issues.

5. Controllers & Smart Control

Controllers determine how your strip lighting operates.

  • Single Colour
    • No controller required
    • Optional dimming modules
  • CCT
    • Required for colour temperature control
  • RGB
    • Required for colour selection and effects

Control Options:

  • Handheld remotes
  • Wall switches
  • Smartphone apps
  • Voice control (Google / Alexa)
  • Integration with sensors or automation systems

Key takeaway:
 Controllers unlock flexibility, automation, and smart home integration.

6. Channels & Installation

Aluminium channels are often essential for a clean, professional finish.

Benefits:

  • Improve heat dissipation
  • Extend lifespan
  • Create a premium, architectural look
  • Diffuse light for a smoother effect

Common Types:

  • Recessed (wing channels) – built into cabinetry
  • Surface-mounted – ideal for retrofits

Finishes:

  • Aluminium (standard)
  • Black or white (premium options)

Diffusers:

  • Typically 15–20% diffusion which help create a uniform and diffused light
  • Reduce glare and hide LED dots

Key Points:
 Channels elevate both performance and aesthetics.

How to Choose the Right LED Strip Light for Your Space

Let's take a closer look at the most common LED strip lighting products, along with their key features and ideal applications. All our strip lighting products are certified, high-quality, and budget-friendly. At Greenhse Technologies, we are committed to delivering reliable and innovative lighting products that you can trust. 

240V Strip Lighting

Best for: Long, continuous runs

Strengths:

  • Long runs up to 50 meters from one supply
  • Low heat, eliminates the need for aluminium profiles
  • No transformers are required, and less wiring
  • Constant and even colour and brightness over full length
  • Thick TPU finish is physically strong 
  • RGB has full colour control and dimming with choice of remotes
  • Single colour can be Triac dimmable
  • RGB Gateway or Smart dimming modules to enable smart control

Applications:

  • Recessed ceilings
  • Large-scale architectural lighting

Options:

  1. RGB or full colour changeable
  2. 3000k Warm white
  3. 4000k  Natural or cool white
  4. 6000k Bright white or Daylight

Long-Run 24V COB

Best for: Clean, dot-free linear lighting

Strengths:

  • COB dotless strip light
  • Up to 20 meters from 1 end with no voltage drop
  • Up to 40 meters with both ends wired
  • Thin and easy to apply in smaller ares
  • Short cut lengths enables flexible installation options
  • Easy to add connectors for short lengths and no waist (up to 4meters)
  • Low power 7,5 Watts /meter
  • IP20 and IP67 Silicon Injected option

Applications:

  • Cabinetry
  • Balustrades
  • Hidden recesses
  • Outdoor (IP67 options)

Options:

  1. IP20 3000k Warm White
  2. IP20 4000k Cool White or Natural white
  3. IP67 3000k Warm White

24V RGB COB

Best for: High-end feature lighting

Strengths:

  • Very bright full colour dotless Lighting
  • Good Cool white option using RGB White
  • Suitable up to 5 meters 
  • 10 meters with both ends connected
  • Easy to add connectors for short lengths and no waste (up to 2 meters)
  • High power 16 Watts /meter
  • Needs Aluminium profile

Applications:

  • Kitchens
  • Bars
  • Shelving
  • Feature recesses

Options:

  1. IP20 16W/m 
  2. IP65 15W/m with Heat-shrink

DISPLAY STRIP LIGHTING 24V 23W/m

  • Very high brightness about 3800 lumens/meter
  • Very High CRI, >90 to give full colour vibrant products
  • Very high Efficiency 165 Lumens/Watt

24V CCT COB

Best for: Adjustable white lighting

Strengths:

  • Very bright dotless Light
  • Warm white to cool white Adjustable (2700k -6500k)
  • Suitable up to 5 meters 
  • 10 meters with both ends connected
  • Easy to add connectors for short lengths and no waste (up to 2 meters)
  • High power 16 Watts /meter
  • Needs Aluminium profile

Applications:

  • Under kitchen cabinets
  • Cabinetry
  • Bars
  • Bulkheads or small recess areas
  • Shelving
  • Architectural features

24V RGB SMD

Best for: Outdoor colour lighting

Strengths:

  • High Density Bright stable full colour
  • Suitable up to 5 meters 
  • 10 meters with both ends connected
  • High power 16 Watts /meter
  • No Aluminium profile needed

Applications:

  • Gardens
  • Outdoor areas
  • Facades
  • Pools and water features

Options:

  1. IP67 Silicon Injected  16W/m 
  2. IP65 gel coated

24V High Lumen SMD

Best for: Performance-driven lighting

Strengths:

  • Very efficient, Bright Strip Lighting
  • Strongest, Longest Lifespan over 50 000 hours
  • 3 OZ high quality Strip Light 
  • 12W/m option does not require aluminium Channel
  • Suitable up to 5 meters 
  • 10 meters with both ends connected
  • Easy to add connectors for short lengths and no waste (up to 2 meters)

Applications:

  • Under cabinets
  • Display lighting
  • Bathroom niches
  • Retail environments

Options:

  1. IP20 23W/m CRI>90 4000k
  2. IP20 23W/m CRI>90 000k
  3. IP65 Silicon gel 20W/m 4000k
  4. IP65 Silicon gel 20W/m 5500k
  5. IP65 Silicon gel 12W/m 3000k
  6. IP65 Silicon gel 12W/m 4000k
  7. IP65 Silicon gel 12W/m 5500k

Neon IP67 Strip

Best for: Signage and creative applications

Strengths:

  • Full programmable colour strip light
  • Can run 5m from one end
  • Supply power to each 10meter
  • Data cable can connect multiple strips together
  • Bluetooth Controllers ()Don’t need wifi connection)
  • 12x12mm Aluminium Support profile

Applications:

  • Signage
  • Feature outlines
  • Commercial installations

Options:

  1. RGB 12x12mm side bend 5m & 3m
  2. RGB 6 x12mm side bend 5m & 3m
  3. CCT 6 x12mm side bend 10m, 5m & 3m
  4. 3000k Warm white 6 x12mm side bend 10m, 5m & 3m

Final Thoughts

Choosing the right strip lighting comes down to three key questions that clear your mind.

  • How long is the run?
  • What colour flexibility do you need?
  • How bright does the space need to be?

Once these are clear, selecting the right product becomes simple for you.

If done correctly, strip lighting doesn't just illuminate a space — it transforms it.

Lighting plays a significant role in the comfort, functionality, and appearance of any space. While many homeowners focus on brightness and colour temperature when choosing lighting, glare is often overlooked. Excessive glare can cause eye strain, discomfort, screen reflections, and uneven lighting throughout a room.

This is where a Low-Glare Downlight can make a significant difference. Designed to reduce harsh light while maintaining excellent illumination, low-glare downlights provide a more comfortable, visually appealing environment in homes and commercial spaces.

In this guide, we’ll explain what low-glare downlights are, how they work, their benefits, and how to choose the best option for your project.

What Is a Low-Glare Downlight?

A Low-Glare Downlight is a recessed LED light specifically designed to minimize direct glare while delivering focused and effective illumination. Unlike standard downlights, which may expose the LED light source directly, low-glare models use deeper recessed lenses, specialized diffusers, or controlled beam angles to reduce visual discomfort.

The goal is simple: provide adequate lighting without creating harsh brightness that can be uncomfortable for occupants.

Why Does Glare Matter?

Glare occurs when a light source is excessively bright compared to its surroundings. This can lead to:

  • Eye fatigue and discomfort
  • Reduced visibility
  • Reflections on televisions and computer screens
  • Visual distractions
  • Reduced room ambience

In residential spaces, glare can make living rooms, bedrooms, home offices, and entertainment areas less comfortable. In commercial settings, it can impact productivity and customer experience.

Choosing Low Glare Downlights helps create a softer and more balanced lighting environment while still maintaining sufficient brightness.

Benefits of Low-Glare Downlights

Improved Visual Comfort

One of the biggest advantages of low-glare lighting is improved comfort. By reducing direct exposure to bright LED chips, occupants experience less eye strain and fatigue, particularly in areas where lights remain on for extended periods.

Better Light Distribution

Many low-glare designs use carefully engineered optics and beam angles to provide a more even spread of light across a room. This helps eliminate harsh hotspots and creates a more consistent lighting effect.

Reduced Screen Reflections

In modern homes, electronic gadgets such as televisions, laptops, tablets, and smartphones can cause glare to become a significant issue. Low-glare lighting helps reduce reflections and improve viewing comfort.

Enhanced Room Aesthetics

Architectural lighting design increasingly favors low-glare fixtures because they create a cleaner, more sophisticated appearance. The recessed light source allows the fixture itself to blend into the ceiling while highlighting the room rather than the light fitting.

Where Should You Use Low-Glare Downlights?

Living Rooms

Living rooms benefit significantly from low-glare lighting because they are often multi-purpose spaces used for relaxing, entertaining, watching television, and reading. Soft, comfortable illumination helps create a welcoming atmosphere.

Bedrooms

In bedrooms, comfort is essential. Low-glare downlights provide sufficient brightness without creating harsh light that can interfere with relaxation.

Home Offices

Home office spaces are very trendy now, and many people do their work from home. Extended screen use can make glare particularly problematic. Low-glare downlights help improve visual comfort while maintaining productivity.

Dining Areas

Proper lighting enhances the dining experience. Low-glare fixtures can create a warm, inviting ambiance without overwhelming the space.

Hotels and Hospitality Venues

Many premium hospitality projects use low-glare lighting to improve guest comfort and create a luxurious environment.

Low-Glare Downlights vs Standard Downlights

While standard downlights may initially appear brighter, low-glare models often provide a superior overall lighting experience by balancing brightness with comfort.

Key Features to Look For

When purchasing a Low-Glare Downlight, consider the following factors:

Beam Angle

A controlled beam angle helps minimize unwanted light spill and improves comfort. Many premium low-glare products use a 60° beam angle for balanced illumination.

Colour Temperature Options

Different spaces require different lighting moods:

  • 3000K Warm White – Comfortable and relaxing
  • 4000K Natural White – Balanced everyday lighting
  • 5000K Bright White – Task-oriented illumination

Selecting the right colour temperature can significantly impact the atmosphere of a room.

Dimming Capability

Dimmable downlights offer greater flexibility, allowing users to adjust brightness based on activities and preferences.

High CRI (Colour Rendering Index)

High CRI lighting ensures colours appear more natural and vibrant, improving the quality of illumination.

/blog/what-do-you-need-to-make-you-home-.lede: Smart homes have become quite popular in Perth; it makes your life easier and more efficient.
/blog/what-do-you-need-to-make-you-home-.bodyHtml:
Smart homes have become quite popular in Perth; it makes your life easier and more efficient. You may remotely control your home lighting and other home essentials. If you want to make your home smart, read the blog, and get to know the What Do You Need To Make Your Home Smart?

To make your home SMART or SMART- READY, you only need 2 things:

1. A good WiFi system.

2. Neutral wires to your switches. There are solutions for homes without Neutral wires, although with Neutral wires, the costs are lower, switches are more stable and options are simpler.

WHAT IS A GOOD WIFI SYSTEM?

A good WiFi system is one which will give you good WiFi coverage throughout your entire home and even outside areas where Smart products may be needed.

It also needs to be quick and allow sufficient devices to be connected. This will prevent the slow functioning of Smart devices and, even more importantly, prevent them from disconnecting and not functioning at all.

A standard home Router is NOT designed to manage a Smart Home. The signal will not be strong, and generally the maximum number of 2.4GHz devices it can connect to will be 12. In addition, it does not manage the signal optimally between devices but will divide the bandwidth 12 times and be extremely slow.

There are many devices available, I can only recommend what works the best from experience, and this is the UBIQUITI range. UBIQUITI U6-LR is a single device that can control a complete home. I use one carefully positioned device to control a double-storey home inside and outside. However, a second Ubiquiti or even a simple WiFi booster can assist in ensuring stronger signals for larger homes or areas further from the Extender.

These devices are designed to be positioned under the ceiling, centrally in a home, and connect to the Router with a data cable using POE (power over ethernet). This data cable must be allowed for when building a new home, or multiple data points for larger or double-storey homes. 

When installing a WiFi Extender, it is important to select separate 2.4Ghz and 5GHz networks and passwords that can be remembered correctly. If you choose the same name and password as your original Router, once the WiFi Extender is connected to the data cable, disable the WiFi on the original Router. All your devices will continue to work without resetting them and will work better.

SELECTING THE SMART PLATFORM: Many suppliers will propose various systems with exorbitant costs and, even worse, discontinued or outdated systems that will not be supported in the future. In fact, it’s quite simple and not expensive. There are a number of proprietary systems on the market, even from good companies, but this does not necessarily make them the best solution. The three leading platforms are Amazon Alexa, Google Home, and Apple Home Kit. These integrate with most Smart products; however, Tuya has become the leader and will completely dominate the Smart market moving forward. 

The factory App, “Tuya” or “Smart Life,” is free. What makes this the most extensive Smart system in the world is that Tuya manufactures the Smart chips in bulk and supplies these to any manufacturing company with the IP and instructions. This ensures the best Smart system in the world and the most competitive. Other companies cannot compete and will likely close, resulting in discontinued systems and no ongoing support. Many companies will be selling Tuya products under their own name, and all of these will work together on one App.

 

SELECTING THE PRODUCT: Buying Tuya products, however, does not guarantee that the product quality is good. It is just as important to purchase good quality products from reputable companies with good warranties and backup which comply with all Australian Electrical certification standards. Many products that use Tuya Chips and promise Smart functions need to be compared as important distinctions exist. This will make the difference between the Smart system working and frustration.

Smart Systems use either WiFi, Bluetooth, or Zigbee

  1. WiFi is the cheapest and will connect directly to your home or office Router.
  2. Bluetooth is the quickest and more stable, working directly with your device, but it requires a Gateway to link it to the Router.
  3. Zigbee is the most expensive and uses the least power consumption, making it suitable for small devices running off batteries.

Tuya works with all three systems; all can be linked and work together to create the most optimal solution with the widest range of products. Most Greenhse products will have a combination of WiFi and Bluetooth to assist with stability and ease of installation. Once you decide to use the Tuya or Smart Life system, your home needs 2 things:

  1. A good WiFi system.
  2. Neutral wires to your switches. There are solutions for homes without Neutral wires, although with Neutral wires, the costs are lower, switches are more stable, and options are simpler.

/blog/why-are-dc-fans-better-than-ac-fan.h1: Why are DC Fans better than AC Fans?
/blog/why-are-dc-fans-better-than-ac-fan.lede: As time goes by, upgrading yourself and the things around you is essential.
/blog/why-are-dc-fans-better-than-ac-fan.bodyHtml:
As time goes by, upgrading yourself and the things around you is essential. There are many types of ceiling fans available on the market and we have found that Australian households are confused about selecting the right fan according to their needs.

This article covers why DC Fans are better than AC Fans. Firstly, what is the difference? DC stands for (direct current) and AC fans are (alternating current).

I hope the information below will help you choose the right fan for your home.

Traditionally ceiling fans run on featured AC motors. Although AC fans are cheaper to manufacture, they are less energy-efficient than DC fans and AC ceiling fans only feature AC motors because residential properties have AC power.

Purchasing a DC fan for a bedroom gives you extremely quiet cooling at the lowest running cost. Up to 8x cheaper than an AC fan and up to 50 times cheaper than ducted air conditioning. The only noise is the sound of the airflow, and no buzzing motors, which softens the external noise of your environment and contributes to better sleeping and health.

 

Comparison between AC fans and DC Fans

• AC fans are up to 85% more expensive to run. A 35W DC fan can produce the same airflow as a 60W AC fan. The AC fan will always draw 60 watts (energy consumption) whereas a DC fan will draw as low as 7W on the lower setting which is used most frequently, saving up to 88% in running costs.

• AC fan motors are noisy, especially at night in a bedroom you will hear the motor hum as opposed to a DC fan which has no motor noise.

• AC fans need in-wall controllers which are more expensive to install; DC fans can be connected to normal wall switches.

• AC fans have limited speed options, normally 3; DC fans have 6 speed options on remote, as well as a reversible option for winter.

• AC fans do not last as long as DC fans which have warranties of 6 Years.

 

Advantages of DC Fans

• Much cheaper to run

• Cheaper and quicker to install

• Quiet motor

• More fan speed options

• Reversible fan for winter

• Long lifespan - 6 Year warranty

Greenhse Technologies have a large range of DC Ceiling fans in Perth in different styles and colors.

Aesthetics and personal choice seem to be the biggest influence when selecting, however, wind flow rate and ceiling height are the most important factors. We have fans with very low depth for low ceilings, 24-watt high brightness lights to suit a single room without compromise, dimmable and colour selectable with remote, as well as full SMART fans.

Thanks for reading our blog. I hope you now understand why DC fans are the more logical choice for modern homes today.

Storage and security

We take reasonable steps to protect your information from misuse, loss and unauthorised access. Payment details are handled by our payment providers and are not stored on our systems.

Access and correction

You can ask us at any time what personal information we hold about you, and ask us to correct or delete it. Contact us on (08) 9297 2969 or through our contact page.

Questions or complaints

If you have a privacy question or believe we have mishandled your information, contact us first and we will work to resolve it. You can also contact the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC) at oaic.gov.au.

Terms & Conditions

These terms apply to purchases from and use of the Greenhse Technologies website. By placing an order you agree to them. Nothing in these terms excludes your rights under the Australian Consumer Law.

Prices and GST

Prices are shown in Australian dollars and exclude GST unless stated otherwise. Prices and specifications are supplier figures and may change without notice; the price at the time you place your order is the price you pay.

Orders and availability

An order is accepted when we confirm it. If an item is unavailable we will contact you with the option of a substitute, a back-order, or a full refund of that item.

Electrical work

In Australia, any 240V mains fitting must be connected by a licensed electrician. Our layout app and lighting advice are planning guides only — quantities, spacings and circuit loads must be verified on site by your licensed electrician before ordering or installation.

Warranty

Our products carry the manufacturer's warranty stated on the product page, in addition to the consumer guarantees under the Australian Consumer Law that cannot be excluded. Warranty claims require proof of purchase and, for hard-wired fittings, evidence of installation by a licensed electrician.

Delivery and risk

Delivery times are estimates. Risk in the goods passes to you on delivery or pickup; title passes when payment is received in full.

Liability

To the extent permitted by law, our liability for any claim is limited to replacement of the goods, resupply of the services, or refund of the price paid.

/returns.html.title: Returns & Shipping | Greenhse Technologies Perth
/returns.html.desc: Returns, refunds and shipping for Greenhse Technologies — your Australian Consumer Law rights, 30-day change of mind returns, and delivery details.
/returns.html.bodyHtml:
Returns & Shipping

Last updated: 25 August 2026

Your consumer rights

Under the Australian Consumer Law, if a product is faulty, not as described, or doesn't do what it should, you are entitled to a repair, replacement or refund — and we honour that without fuss. Bring the product back with your proof of purchase, or call us and we'll sort out the return.

Change of mind

Changed your mind or over-ordered? Return unused items in their original, resaleable packaging within 30 days of purchase with your receipt and we will refund or exchange them. Items cut to length (such as strip lighting sold per metre), special orders, and fittings that have been installed cannot be returned for change of mind.

How to return

  • In store — 5/1 Locke Ln, Ellenbrook WA 6069, Mon–Fri 8AM–5PM.
  • By post — call (08) 9297 2969 or use the contact page first so we can raise the return and give you the address details. For change-of-mind returns, return postage is at your cost; for faulty items we cover it.

Shipping

We ship across Perth and WA, with freight calculated at checkout based on size and destination. Local pickup from our Ellenbrook showroom is free. Large or fragile fittings may ship by courier with signature on delivery. If an item arrives damaged, contact us within 48 hours with a photo and we will replace it.

Refunds

Refunds go back to your original payment method once the return is received and checked, normally within 5 business days.
